sentences.text: Tehuelchesaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 147 million years ago, in what is now South America.
This moderately large animal measured approximately 15 meters in length, 6 meters in height, and weighed an estimated 10 tonnes.
All dorsal vertebrae and all presacral vertebrae possess opisthocoelous centra, a trait that distinguishes it from related genera like Barapasaurus and Patagosaurus.
A unique feature of its skeleton is that the dorsal neural spines are lateromedially narrow and anteroposteriorly elongated.
The forelimb anatomy includes a short, robust humerus with strongly expanded ends and a thin middle shaft, while the anterior dorsal ribs are shaped like planks.
As a camarasauromorph, it also possessed an acromion process located near the midpoint of the scapular body and a puboischiadic contact reaching half the length of the pubis.
Skin impressions reveal that the animal was covered by flat, hexagonal scales arranged adjacently to form a rosette pattern, unlike the overlapping scales of modern lizards.
Researchers note a possible derived trait in the anterior dorsal vertebrae: the presence of sharp posterior pleurocoels.
The genus and its type species, Tehuelchesaurus benitezii, were named by Rich, Vickers-Rich, Gimenez, Cuneo, Puerta, and Vacca in 1999.
The name honors the Tehuelche people, who are native to the Chubut province of Argentina where the fossils were found, and specifically commemorates Aldo Benitez, who discovered the holotype.

Fossil remains were discovered in the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation, yielding a 50% complete skeleton (MPEF-PV 1125) that includes 10 articulated presacral vertebrae, 4 sacral vertebrae, various ribs, right scapulocoracoid, right humerus, left radius and ulna, right ilium fragment, right pubis, left pubis fragment, left ischium, right ischial diaphysis, both femurs, and skin impressions.
Indeterminate theropod teeth were found alongside the main fossil remains.
Based on bone measurements including a 1.14 m humerus and 1.53 m femur, the animal was estimated to be about 15 meters long.
A 2019 analysis by Mannion et al. classified Tehuelchesaurus as a basal member of Turiasauria.
Recent phylogenetic analysis places the genus within Camarasauromorpha, related to Camarasaurus and Galveosaurus, but outside Titanosauriformes.
Research indicates that Tehuelchesaurus forms a distinct clade with Galvesaurus, a grouping supported by two unambiguous shared derived characteristics.

The placement of both genera as camarasauromorphs more derived than Europasaurus is supported by shared traits including plank-shaped anterior dorsal ribs and a lateral femoral protuberance, as well as undivided spinopostzygapophyseal laminae.
Tehuelchesaurus is considered a basal macronarian that is more derived than Europasaurus but falls outside the clade containing Tastavinisaurus, Janenschia, and advanced camarasauromorphs.

It differs from Omeisaurus in the shape of the coracoid, radius, and ulna, as well as the pubis and ischium, and possesses dorsal vertebrae with deep pseudopleurocoels and opistocoelous centra, unlike Barapasaurus and Patagosaurus.
Tehuelchesaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 147 million years ago, in what is now South America.
